title: Bulk response integrity notice and tenant validation playbook
content:
Background:
We observed a class of incidents where high-volume batch/streaming requests touching cached KV prefixes returned mixed-response fragments for a subset of tenants. The problem manifested as duplicated or truncated tokens in bulk generation responses (primarily multi-request batch jobs and some streaming sessions), affecting integrity guarantees for those requests. This draft is a combined customer-facing status update and a self-serve validation playbook tenants can use to confirm whether they were impacted, what evidence to collect, and which remediation options are available.

Goal of this doc:
- Provide a concise status page-ready blurb for customers
- Offer a verification checklist customers can run without engineering help
- Outline recommended customer actions and our remediation commitments
- Describe root cause at a level suitable for technical product teams

Quick summary (for status page / short update):
- What happened: Between 2029-07-08 21:14 UTC and 2029-07-09 02:42 UTC, a serving runtime regression caused intermittent response integrity issues for a small fraction of high-throughput tenants.
- Who was affected: ~0.6% of active tenants by request volume; concentrated on large batched/streaming workloads that used prefix caching.
- Impact: Some generated responses contained duplicated tokens, truncated sequences, or token mis-ordering in batch outputs. No data exfiltration or tenant cross-contamination was detected.
- Current status: Mitigation rolled out 2029-07-09 03:10 UTC. Ongoing validation and tail-risk remediation in progress.

Suggested status page blurb (short):
We identified and mitigated an issue causing intermittent duplication/truncation in some bulk generation responses for a small number of tenants. The fix was deployed and we are validating outputs. If you see suspect responses, please follow the verification steps below and contact your account team.

Technical timeline (candidate for postmortem appendix):
- 2029-07-08 20:58 UTC — Canary regression introduced during kernel selection change (deploy RI-3457)
- 2029-07-08 21:14 UTC — First error spike observed in internal anomaly detectors (duplicate token ratio)
- 2029-07-08 21:20 UTC — Ops paged; initial scope estimate: small subset of batched workloads
- 2029-07-08 21:40 UTC — Temporary routing preference applied away from affected canary pool
- 2029-07-09 01:55 UTC — Root cause hypothesized: stale per-connection prefix-state reuse combined with aggressive KV cache eviction in the new kernel path
- 2029-07-09 03:10 UTC — Rollback of RI-3457 and targeted restart of affected serving hosts completed
- 2029-07-09 04:30 UTC — First customer validation pass completed internally; false-positive rate low
- 2029-07-15 12:00 UTC — Additional hardening PRs and test coverage merged; extended validation plan ongoing

Root cause (non-sensitive summary):
A change to the kernel selection heuristics inadvertently re-used certain prefix state objects across distinct request contexts under high-concurrency batching. In normal operation those objects are immutable for a request; the regression allowed transient sharing when combined with a change in the KV cache eviction timing. The result: a small percentage of batched/streaming requests read prefix buffers that had been partially recycled, producing duplicated or truncated token sequences in the final output.

Customer verification checklist (self-serve, low-effort):
1) Identify suspicious requests
   - Look for generation jobs or streams that returned duplicated phrases, truncated assertions, or mis-ordered tokens between 2029-07-08 20:00 UTC and 2029-07-09 06:00 UTC.
2) Collect evidence
   - Export 3–10 example response pairs (expected vs observed) and note the request_id and timestamp for each.
   - For batch jobs, include the input array index and the per-item request_id.
3) Run quick integrity diff (if you have a replay harness)
   - Re-play the same inputs against a non-affected model variant or against a small local replica (if available) and compare tokenization boundaries.
4) Check for correlated patterns
   - Are issues concentrated in jobs that used larger batch sizes (>32) or streaming sessions with prefix caching?
   - Any correlation with short inter-request gaps (<50ms)?
5) If you confirm impact, file the evidence bundle to us via the incident upload link below (or share with your CS rep).

Remediation options for customers (recommended order):
- Option A (if you need immediate correctness): Re-run affected batch jobs against a pinned stable model variant or with batch_size reduced to <=16. This avoids the kernel selection path that triggered the issue.
- Option B (if re-run is costly): Request a tenant-specific audit from Redwood; we will scan stored logs and provide a signed integrity statement for the affected window. This is a paid forensic service for large enterprise customers, but we will provide a limited scan free for verified-impact cases.
- Option C (for streaming): Re-open streaming sessions to refresh connection state; we can provide guidance to replay with explicit session resets.

What we (Redwood) are doing now:
- Deployed immediate rollback to the prior kernel selector and restarted impacted hosts (completed 2029-07-09 03:10 UTC).
- Running a targeted log-scan over all candidate tenants for the 8-hour window to classify impacted sessions (in progress).
- Added unit/integration tests that reproduce high-concurrency prefix-state scenarios and included them in CI gating.
- Shipping a follow-up patch that prevents prefix-object reuse and hardens KV eviction synchronization (merged 2029-07-15).
- Offering a tenant-scope integrity scan and replay assistance for customers with confirmed impact.

Customer-facing escalation and SLA options:
- If you require a formal SLA credit evaluation, open a support ticket with subject: "RI-7214: Integrity impact evidence" and include the evidence bundle. Our CS team will initiate an SLA assessment within 48 hours.
- For enterprise customers with Dedicated/Private deployments, we will coordinate a more thorough local audit and, if necessary, a tailored rollback/replay plan.

Suggested internal notes for CS reps (do not include all in public status):
- Prioritize customers with high batch volumes and legal/compliance use-cases (doc classification, contract generation).
- Offer to run a free sample scan for accounts that provide 3 example request_id values.
- Avoid technical jargon in initial outreach; use the short summary copy, then provide the verification checklist if they request technical next steps.

FAQ (customer-centric):
Q: Did this affect data privacy or cause cross-tenant data leakage?
A: No. We found no evidence of tenant crossover. The issue was limited to internal reuse of buffer state within a single host and did not leak data across tenants.

Q: Will I be reimbursed for affected requests?
A: Requests that are confirmed impacted by the integrity regression are eligible for credit under our incident compensation policy. Submit evidence and we will process credits per the SLA.

Q: How can I prevent this from hitting my workloads?
A: Short-term: reduce batch size or pin to a verified stable model variant. Long-term: Redwood will provide updated runtime defaults and tests; Dedicated customers can opt into the hardened kernel selector immediately.

Action items for publishing this draft:
- [CS] Convert the "Suggested status page blurb" to a StatusPage update and publish once internal verification completes.
- [SRE] Share a redacted timeline for external postmortem and confirm the final mitigation PR number.
- [Product] Coordinate a short customer webinar covering what happened and how to validate results (optional).

Contact & escalation:
- Primary CS contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- On-call SRE: Daniel Romero (slack: @danielr, pager: on-call)
- Incident ticket: JIRA-RI-7214

Notes to self / draft footers:
- Keep language conservative: avoid definitive claims until full log-scan completes.
- We may want to include a simple example diff in the final postmortem appendix (one before/after response pair).
- Consider providing a small replay tool snippet for customers who want to verify locally (engineering to vet).

End of draft.
